body.title: bug: teams setting permission description for PRs is unclear
body.body:
### Can you reproduce the bug on the Forgejo test instance?

No, I've tried it and the problem is not present there

### Description

1. create a team
2. set permissions: Code - no access, Issues - write, Pull requests - READ

What.I noticed strange that Pull Request has a description saying: "Read: Reading and create pull requests.".

So I was thinking how it's even possible to create a PR without access into a code. Hopefully it's not, button is disabled, but that description makes me wonder. 

Can we do a condition description based on what I check in "code" section?

bellow

body.title: enh: real-time events in PRs or issues
body.body:
### Existing problems this enhancement addresses

Open issue or pull request page, new comments, edited comments, and reactions don’t appear until the page is reloaded. For example, when a bot edits its “working…” comment to show the result, the page still shows the old comment.

Reloading can discard a half-written comment and reset the scroll position. Without live updates, you may only notice activity through notifications.

The same goes for other interactive elements on the PR page (linked related issues bellow).

### Enhancement description

Workarounds:
- Reload the page
- Have the bot mention the person in its first comment to trigger a notification
- I haven’t checked whether editing a comment sends a notification

### Details and notes

Forgejo 16.0.5+gitea-1.22.0, self-hosted.

Probably related:
- #12906 - the same problem with the checks and merge box.
- #13511 - /user/events (EventSource) is the only pushed update, covers only the navbar, and has been reported broken on Forgejo 15–16.

body.title: bug: git over ssh broken with default config if forgejo and sshd have differing XDG_RUNTIME_DIR
body.body:
### Can you reproduce the bug on the Forgejo test instance?

No, I can't try it on the test instance for some reason

### Description

After updating to https://codeberg.org/slink/forgejo/commit/512c06974d14d8fdcb7a214c8e506057dbd981b8, which is based on 08ba2d68b6d2d4052d8dae16e15cb5be4ad01897, git over ssh was no longer possible:

```
$ git push
Forgejo: Internal Server Connection Error
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.

Please make sure you have the correct access rights
and the repository exists.
$ git pull
Forgejo: Internal Server Connection Error
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.

Please make sure you have the correct access rights
and the repository exists.
```

I tracked down the reason by adding `set >/tmp/env && /usr/bin/strace -o /tmp/tr -f ` to the `command` for my ssh key and found the following:

```
$ grep -E 'internal.sock|Forge' /tmp/tr
1599397 connect(4, {sa_family=AF_UNIX, sun_path="/run/user/1001/forgejo/internal.sock"}, 39) = -1 ENOENT (No such file or directory)
1599397 write(2, "Forgejo: Internal Server Connect"..., 42) = 42
1599397 connect(4, {sa_family=AF_UNIX, sun_path="/run/user/1001/forgejo/internal.sock"}, 39) = -1 ENOENT (No such file or directory)
$ grep XDG /tmp/env
XDG_RUNTIME_DIR='/run/user/1001'
```

forgejo itself is started via systemD with the `RunTimeDirectory` as in the example

https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/src/commit/adfdb1a53298d953669fcf49d61393a32b256fb5/contrib/systemd/forgejo.service#L59

```
# grep -vE '^#|^$' /etc/systemd/system/forgejo.service
[Unit]
Description=Forgejo (Beyond coding. We forge.)
After=syslog.target
After=network.target
Wants=postgresql.service
After=postgresql.service
[Service]
RestartSec=2s
Type=simple
User=git
Group=git
WorkingDirectory=/var/lib/forgejo/
RuntimeDirectory=forgejo
RuntimeDirectoryMode=0750
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/forgejo web --config /etc/forgejo/app.ini
Restart=always
Environment=USER=git HOME=/home/git FORGEJO_WORK_DIR=/var/lib/forgejo
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

The socket gets created as `/run/forgejo/internal.sock`

```
# ls -rtl /run/forgejo/internal.sock 
srwxr-xr-x 1 git git 0  8. Okt  11:56 /run/forgejo/internal.sock
```

So clearly the problem is that systemD starts forgejo without `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` being set, but when coming in via `sshd`, it is set. This does not work with the default from cda3aca4c92e775ccfeec66648a061e05f823b54 / #14148

While the workaround is trivial (to set `INTERNAL_LISTENER_PATH` in the `.ini` to the right absolute path), I wonder if the default should be changed to cause less friction?

### Forgejo Version

08ba2d68b6d2d4052d8dae16e15cb5be4ad01897

### How are you running Forgejo?

self built self hosted

### Logs

_No response_

### Database

PostgreSQL
